reason: The cited evidence (E1) only reports that tensile-compression asymmetry in bulk FeNiCrCoCu increases with temperature and Cu content; it provides no data on interfacial diffusion layers, their effect on dislocations/twins, or any link to wear resistance. The key premises about the interfacial layer, its formation, and its mechanistic role are entirely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: FeNiCrCoCu exhibits tensile-compression asymmetry that increases with temperature and Cu content
A Cu-enriched interfacial diffusion layer can form between FeNiCrCoCu coating and a metal substrate at high temperature
Such an interfacial layer suppresses dislocation slip and twin formation at the interface
Suppressing dislocation/twin activity reduces tensile-compression asymmetry
Reduced asymmetry enhances overall wear resistance under high-temperature loading
